We're here to help.Contact UsOverviewYellowstone National Park, Wyoming ToursYellowstone, America's first national park and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is a spectacular wilderness of geological wonders and abundant wildlife. It sits atop a volcanic hotspot, giving rise to more than half of the world's active geysers and a mesmerizing array of hot springs, mud pots, and fumaroles. This vast, two-million-acre park is a sanctuary for some of the continent's most iconic animals, including bison, elk, wolves, and bears, all thriving in their natural habitat.A visit to Yellowstone is an awe-inspiring experience that showcases the raw power and beauty of nature. From the thunderous eruptions of Old Faithful to the vibrant colors of the Grand Prismatic Spring and the breathtaking views of the Grand Canyon of the Yellowstone, the park offers a continuous series of stunning sights. Yellowstone is a place of profound beauty and scientific significance, promising a journey you will never forget.Top Things to Do in Yellowstone National Park, WyomingWitness the Eruption of Old FaithfulNo visit to Yellowstone is complete without seeing Old Faithful, the park's most famous geyser. It erupts on a predictable schedule, though not exactly on the hour, shooting a column of hot water and steam high into the air. The visitor center provides an estimated eruption time.Tip: Arrive early to get a good spot and take time to explore the walking paths around the Upper Geyser Basin to see other smaller but equally beautiful geysers and hot springs.Marvel at the Grand Prismatic SpringVisit the Grand Prismatic Spring, the largest hot spring in the United States. Its vibrant, rainbow-like colors are created by heat-loving bacteria, and the resulting sight is absolutely spectacular. The best views are from the designated boardwalks or the nearby elevated trail.Tip: The colors are most brilliant on a sunny day. Take the short, uphill trail to the Grand Prismatic Spring Overlook for an iconic, panoramic view.Hike to the Grand Canyon of the YellowstoneExplore the Grand Canyon of the Yellowstone, a massive canyon carved by the Yellowstone River. The canyon features two magnificent waterfalls, the Upper and Lower Falls, and offers numerous viewpoints from both the North and South Rims.Tip: For an incredible view of the Lower Falls, hike down the steep switchbacks of the Brink of the Lower Falls Trail.Drive Through Lamar Valley for Wildlife ViewingTake a scenic drive through the Lamar Valley, often called the "Serengeti of North America." This vast, open valley is one of the best places in the park to spot large herds of bison and elk, as well as wolves, bears, and other predators, especially during dawn and dusk.Tip: Bring binoculars or a spotting scope to get a better view of the wildlife from a safe distance.Explore the Terraces of Mammoth Hot SpringsWander along the boardwalks of Mammoth Hot Springs, a unique geological formation of travertine terraces created by hot water bubbling up from underground. The site's stark, bleached-out landscapes contrast with its vivid, colorful bacterial mats.Tip: The terraces are beautiful in any weather, but the colors can seem more vibrant on a cloudy day.Visit the Yellowstone Lake AreaEnjoy the serene beauty of Yellowstone Lake, the largest high-elevation lake in North America. The lake area offers opportunities for boating, fishing, and hiking, with beautiful views of the surrounding mountains and forests.Tip: Consider a scenic walk along the lake's shores or visit the historic Lake Yellowstone Hotel for a glimpse of the park's early history.Previous SlideNext SlideThings to Know Before You GoIt is a Geothermal Wonderland: Yellowstone is home to the world's largest collection of geysers and other hydrothermal features. The most famous is Old Faithful, which erupts on a predictable schedule, but don't miss the stunning colors of the Grand Prismatic Spring and the unique mud pots and terraces found throughout the park.You Will See Wild Animals, but Keep Your Distance: The park is home to the largest concentration of wild mammals in the contiguous U.S. and is famous for its herds of bison and elk, as well as grizzly bears and wolves. It is essential to stay at least 100 yards away from bears and wolves and 25 yards away from all other wildlife.Planning Ahead is Essential: At over 3,400 square miles, Yellowstone is huge. Roads are slow, and "bison jams" can cause major delays. It is best to book lodging and campsites far in advance, and to arrive at popular attractions early in the morning to find parking. Always stay on designated boardwalks and trails to avoid stepping into dangerous thermal areas.Need advice, assistance, or a deal? We're here to help.Contact UsNeed advice, assistance, or a deal?
